operator_rule: 2026-11-07 — Finviz cache first (<=30 min), a fresh Schwab/Alpaca/moomoo quote second, the stored mark only flagged stale. Never yfinance as a price.
rule: SHRINK-ONLY ratchet, enforced by tests/test_ticker_price_source_filter_lq1695_20261109.py. Every SQL statement under scripts/ that names ticker_prices and is not a docstring must carry `sql_source_allowed()` (or a recognised source constraint) unless it appears here with a kind and a reason. Editing a statement changes its hash, so a re-baseline is a visible edit, never a silent one. An entry whose statement disappears, or that gains the predicate, fails the guard: delete the entry. Nothing may be ADDED without a reason that a reviewer can check against the module.

kinds.writer: writes or upserts ticker_prices rows. It must read every source it is about to overwrite or compare against; a source filter would make it blind to the rows it maintains.
kinds.admin: quarantine / scrub / repair of corrupt rows. It must see every row it grades, including the banned sources, or it cannot repair them.
kinds.measurement: grades store quality or replays history (shadow replay, counterfactual ledger, data quality). The historical series is the object measured, not a price served to a signal.
kinds.presence: answers only 'does this symbol have any price row?' (coverage, backfill eligibility, discovery). It never returns a close, so a filtered answer would change eligibility rather than serve a stale price.
kinds.source_grading: compares sources against each other (source litmus). Excluding a source would delete the evidence it grades.

entries.reason: Data-quality audit: it grades the store's own rows (duplicates, spikes, gaps) per symbol/date. Filtering would hide the yfinance history it exists to report on.
entries.sql: SELECT symbol, price_date, max(close_price) AS close_price FROM ticker_prices WHERE symbol = ANY(%s) AND price_date > CURRENT_DATE - 220 GROUP BY symbol, price_date

entries.reason: Shadow replay of a past defense decision: reconstructs the closes the system actually had on each date. A source filter would rewrite history.
entries.sql: SELECT symbol, (array_agg(close_price ORDER BY price_date DESC))[1] AS last, avg(close_price) FILTER (WHERE price_date > %s) AS dma, count(*) n FROM ticker_prices ...
